question_text: What is the essential requirement for an invention to be patentable under the European Patent Convention (EPC)?

answer_choices.c: The invention must have a technical character or technicality.
answer_choices.a: The invention must be a mathematical method.
answer_choices.b: The invention must be a business method.
answer_choices.d: The invention must be a computer-implemented method.

answer justification: According to the text, an invention may be an invention within the meaning of Article 52(1) EPC if it has a technical character or technicality. Therefore, the essential requirement for an invention to be patentable under the EPC is that it has a technical character or technicality.
source: Article 52(1) EPC 1973 and the text provided.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for considering an activity to be a non-invention "as such" within the meaning of Article 52(2) and (3) EPC 1973?

answer_choices.a: The activity is carried out using technical means.
answer_choices.b: The activity is a purely abstract concept.
answer_choices.c: The activity is so familiar that its technical character tends to be overlooked.
answer_choices.d: The activity is a non-obvious technical solution to a technical problem.

answer justification: According to the text, activities falling within the concept of a non-invention "as such" would typically represent purely abstract concepts devoid of any technical implications. Therefore, option B is a reason for considering an activity to be a non-invention "as such" within the meaning of Article 52(2) and (3) EPC 1973.

question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a mathematical method or algorithm?

answer_choices.a: It is carried out on numbers and provides a result also in numerical form.
answer_choices.b: It is an abstract concept prescribing how to operate on the numbers.
answer_choices.c: It is a technical process.
answer_choices.d: It produces a direct technical result.

answer justification: According to the text, a mathematical method or algorithm is carried out on numbers (whatever these numbers may represent) and also provides a result also in numerical form. Therefore, option A is a characteristic of a mathematical method or algorithm.

question_text: Which of the following is a necessary condition for a claim to a computer program to avoid exclusion from patentability under Art. 52(2) and (3) EPC?

answer_choices.a: The claim explicitly mentions the use of a computer or a computer-readable storage medium.
answer_choices.b: The claim specifies no more than "Program X on a computer-readable storage medium," or "A method of operating a computer according to program X."
answer_choices.c: The program has the potential of achieving a further technical effect when run and thus also contributes to the technical character of the claimed subject matter.
answer_choices.d: The claim does not specify any technical effect on a physical entity in the real world.

question_text: What is the correct interpretation of the term "technical" with respect to computer programs according to opinion G 3/08?

answer_choices.a: Any technical considerations are sufficient to confer technical character on claimed subject -matter.
answer_choices.b: Technical considerations are not sufficient to confer technical character on claimed subject -matter, and further technical considerations are required.
answer_choices.c: Technical considerations are not required to confer technical character on claimed subject -matter.
answer_choices.d: Technical considerations are sufficient to confer technical character on claimed subject -matter, but only if the specific use of the system as a whole is considered.

answer justification: According to the text, opinion G 3/08 explicitly rejected the position that any technical considerations are sufficient to confer technical character on claimed subject -matter. Therefore, option B is the correct answer.
source: opinion G 3/08, point 13.5 of the Reasons.

question_text: Which of the following is not excluded from patentability under Article 52(2) and (3) EPC 1973?

answer_choices.a: Methods for doing business
answer_choices.b: Methods for playing games
answer_choices.c: Methods for performing mental acts
answer_choices.d: Methods for determining an efficient schedule for a plurality of scheduled agents in a telephone call centre

answer justification: According to the text, methods for doing business, methods for playing games, and methods for performing mental acts are excluded from patentability under Article 52(2) and (3) EPC 1973. However, the Enlarged Board in G 1/19 stated that the negative assessment under Article 56 EPC was (or could have been) based on the lack of a technical effect by the simulation rather than on the non-technical nature of the simulated system. Therefore, a method for determining an efficient schedule for a plurality of scheduled agents in a telephone call centre is not excluded from patentability under Article 52(2) and (3) EPC 1973.

question_text: Which of the following is a presentation of information in the sense of Article 52(2)(d) EPC?

answer_choices.a: A record carrier characterised by having functional data recorded thereon
answer_choices.b: A data structure defined in terms which inherently comprise the technical features of the system in which the record carrier is operative
answer_choices.c: A program recorded on a carrier
answer_choices.d: A data structure product

answer justification: According to the text, a record carrier characterised by having functional data recorded thereon is a presentation of information as such and hence excluded from patentability by Art. 52(2)(d) and (3) EPC 1973.

question_text: Which of the following is the reason for the exclusion of medical methods from patentability under Article 53(c) EPC?

answer_choices.a: The methods are not susceptible of industrial application.
answer_choices.b: The methods are not carried out on a physical entity.
answer_choices.c: The methods are not described in mathematical terms.
answer_choices.d: The methods are excluded mainly in the light of public health considerations.

answer justification: According to the text, medical methods are excluded from patentability mainly in the light of public health considerations. Therefore, option D is the reason for the exclusion of medical methods from patentability under Article 53(c) EPC.

question_text: Which of the following is the definition of the concept of "morality" according to the EPC?

answer_choices.a: The belief that some behaviour is right and acceptable whereas other behaviour is wrong, this belief being founded on the totality of the accepted norms which are deeply rooted in a particular culture.
answer_choices.b: The belief that some behaviour is wrong and unacceptable whereas other behaviour is right, this belief being founded on the totality of the accepted norms which are deeply rooted in a particular culture.
answer_choices.c: The belief that some behaviour is right and acceptable whereas other behaviour is wrong, this belief being founded on the totality of the accepted norms which are deeply rooted in a particular society.
answer_choices.d: The belief that some behaviour is wrong and unacceptable whereas other behaviour is right, this belief being founded on the totality of the accepted norms which are deeply rooted in a particular society.

question_text: What is the current interpretation of the exclusion of plants exclusively obtained by means of an essentially biological process from patentability under Article 53(b) EPC?

answer_choices.b: The exclusion is not in conflict with the Implementing Regulations as interpreted by the Enlarged Board of Appeal in decisions G 2/12 and G 2/13.
answer_choices.c: The exclusion is in conflict with the Biotech Directive as put forward in the notice of the European Commission on certain articles of Directive 98/44/EC.
answer_choices.d: The exclusion is not in conflict with the Biotech Directive as put forward in the notice of the European Commission on certain articles of Directive 98/44/EC.

question_text: What is the definition of "treatment by surgery" according to the Enlarged Board of Appeal in G 1/07?

answer_choices.a: Treatment by surgery is limited to surgical methods pursuing a therapeutic purpose.
answer_choices.b: Treatment by surgery refers to the nature of the treatment rather than its purpose.
answer_choices.c: Treatment by surgery is limited to surgical methods for the purpose of diagnosis.
answer_choices.d: Treatment by surgery is limited to surgical methods for the purpose of research.

answer justification: In G 1/07, the Enlarged Board of Appeal concluded that neither the legal history nor the object and purpose of the exclusions from patentability in Art. 53(c) EPC would justify a limitation of the term "treatment by surgery" to curative surgery. Such a limitation would be contrary to the ordinary understanding of the word "surgery" as referring to the nature of the treatment rather than its purpose.

question_text: Which of the following is true about a claim encompassing a surgical step under Article 53(c) EPC?

answer_choices.a: The claim cannot be left unamended.
answer_choices.b: The claim can be left unamended.
answer_choices.c: The claim can be amended to omit the surgical step.
answer_choices.d: The claim cannot be amended to omit the surgical step.

answer justification: According to the text, a claim encompassing an embodiment which is excluded from patentability under Article 53(c) EPC cannot be left unamended.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for a claimed method to be non-patentable under Article 53(c) EPC?

answer_choices.a: The method has both therapeutic and non-therapeutic indications, and the therapeutic element is inseparably associated with the non-therapeutic element.
answer_choices.b: The method has both therapeutic and non-therapeutic indications, but the therapeutic effects can be clearly distinguished from the non-therapeutic use and are not covered by the subject-matter of the claim.
answer_choices.c: The method has only therapeutic indications, but the therapeutic element is not an essential part of the claimed method.
answer_choices.d: The method has only non-therapeutic indications.

question_text: Which of the following steps is not considered when assessing the diagnostic character of a method of diagnosing Alzheimer's disease in a living subject?

answer_choices.a: Data collection
answer_choices.b: Data processing using an automated apparatus
answer_choices.c: Adjustment or preparation of the apparatus
answer_choices.d: Comparison of collected data with standard values

answer justification: According to the text, data processing using an automated apparatus is not part of the examination phase which involves the data collection phase, but it results from a subsequent, technical step, intermediate between the data collection and the comparison of these collected data with standard values. Therefore, data processing using an automated apparatus is not considered when assessing the diagnostic character of the method.
source: Article I.B.4 of the law text.

question_text: What is the purpose of Article 54(1) EPC?

answer_choices.a: To allow the state of the art to be patented again.
answer_choices.b: To prevent the state of the art being patented again.
answer_choices.c: To define the prior art, the relevant part of that art, and the content of that relevant art.
answer_choices.d: To compare the invention with the prior art thus defined, and see whether the invention differs from it.

answer justification: According to the text, the purpose of Article 54(1) EPC is to prevent the state of the art being patented again.

question_text: What is the minimum requirement for a written description to be considered as having been made available to the public?

answer_choices.a: It was possible for the public to gain knowledge of its content with an obligation of confidentiality restricting the use or dissemination of such knowledge.
answer_choices.b: It was possible for the public to gain knowledge of its content without any obligation of confidentiality restricting the use or dissemination of such knowledge.
answer_choices.c: It was possible for the public to gain knowledge of its content with an obligation of confidentiality restricting the use or dissemination of such knowledge, but only if a member of the public actually saw the document or knew that it was available.
answer_choices.d: It was possible for the public to gain knowledge of its content with an obligation of confidentiality restricting the use or dissemination of such knowledge, but only if there were particular reasons for analysing the product.

question_text: According to the text, which of the following is a reason for considering an oral disclosure as having been made available to the public?

answer_choices.a: The oral disclosure was based on a written disclosure published some years earlier.
answer_choices.b: The oral disclosure was made at a public conference held some years earlier.
answer_choices.c: The oral disclosure was made at a public conference held some days before the priority date.
answer_choices.d: The oral disclosure was made to an audience of some 100 to 200 persons.

answer justification: According to the text, an oral disclosure is considered as having been made available to the public if it was made at a public conference held some days before the priority date, and there was no bar of confidentiality restricting its use or dissemination.

question_text: What is the definition of public prior use according to the EPC?

answer_choices.a: A prior use that is made available to the public by means of a written or oral description, by use, or in any other way, before the date of filing of the European patent application.
answer_choices.b: A prior use that is made available to the public by means of a written or oral description, by use, or in any other way, after the date of filing of the European patent application.
answer_choices.c: A prior use that is made available to the public by means of a written or oral description, by use, or in any other way, after the date of grant of the European patent application.
answer_choices.d: A prior use that is made available to the public by means of a written or oral description, by use, or in any other way, before the date of grant of the European patent application.

answer justification: According to the text, public prior use refers to everything made available to the public by means of a written or oral description, by use, or in any other way, before the date of filing of the European patent application.

question_text: What is the principle set out in G 1/92 that makes manufacturing processes available to the public within the meaning of Art. 54(2) EPC 1973?

answer_choices.a: The fact that the manufacturing processes are explicitly explained to visitors.
answer_choices.b: The fact that the manufacturing processes are carried out in a public place.
answer_choices.c: The fact that direct, unlimited and unambiguous access to any particular information regarding the manufacturing processes is possible.
answer_choices.d: The fact that the manufacturing processes are carried out by skilled persons.

answer justification: According to the text, the principle set out in G 1/92 is that it is the fact that direct, unlimited and unambiguous access to any particular information regarding the manufacturing processes is possible that makes these processes available to the public within the meaning of Art. 54(2) EPC 1973.
source: I.C.3. Availability to the public, 103, referring to T 947/99.

question_text: In the context of the EPC, which of the following is a condition for a disclosure to be considered made available to the public?

answer_choices.a: The disclosure was made to a person under an obligation to maintain secrecy.
answer_choices.b: The disclosure was made to a person who did not breach the obligation to maintain secrecy.
answer_choices.c: The disclosure was made to a person who was not under an obligation to maintain secrecy.
answer_choices.d: The disclosure was made to a person who was under an obligation to maintain secrecy and breached that obligation.

answer justification: According to the text, a disclosure is considered made available to the public if there is no bar of confidentiality restricting the use or dissemination of such knowledge. If the person who was able to gain knowledge of the invention was under an obligation to maintain secrecy, the invention cannot be said to have been made available to the public, provided the person did not breach that obligation. Therefore, option A is a condition for a disclosure to be considered made available to the public.

question_text: What is the standard of proof to be applied to prior public use objections under Article 100 EPC?

question_text: Which of the following is not a correct statement about the interpretation of the "whole contents" of an earlier document in the context of novelty under the EPC?

answer_choices.a: The "whole contents" of an earlier document does not include features which are equivalents of features in a later document.
answer_choices.b: The "whole contents" of an earlier document does not include features which can be derived from the document by applying the document's teaching mutatis mutandis.

answer_choices.d: The "whole contents" of an earlier document includes features which are derivable from the document by applying the document's teaching mutatis mutandis.

Therefore, option C is not a correct statement about the interpretation of the "whole contents" of an earlier document in the context of novelty under the EPC.
source: Novelty section of the law text.

question_text: In the context of chemical inventions and selection inventions, what is the question that arises when a general term in the state of the art is used?

answer_choices.b: Whether the general term used in the citation discloses the subject -matter defined by the special term in the claim?

question_text: Which of the following is the correct approach for deciding selection novelty according to T 133/92?

answer_choices.d: The approach is to consider the claimed group of compounds as essentially resulting from omitting those parts of a larger group of compounds which a skilled person would have immediately considered as being less interesting than the rest.

answer justification: According to the text, the board in T 133/92 found that the proper approach for deciding selection novelty is to consider availability in the light of a particular document. Therefore, option C is the correct answer.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for excluding a combination of alloying elements from patentability under Article 52(2) and (3) EPC 1973?

answer_choices.a: The combination is not a technical process.
answer_choices.b: The combination does not produce a direct technical result.
answer_choices.c: The combination is not carried out on a physical entity.
answer_choices.d: The combination is not described in the prior art.

answer justification: According to the text, in the case of an alloy composition, a disclosure of a combination of the different alloying elements within the claimed ranges is necessary for a finding of lack of novelty. Since the different alloying elements interact with each other to form precipitates and solid solutions, their content ranges are not to be considered in isolation but in combination. Therefore, if the combination is not described in the prior art, it is not patentable under Article 52(2) and (3) EPC 1973.
source: I.C.6. Chemical inventions and selection inventions, paragraph 153.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for excluding a confidential disclosure in the application as a starting point for the assessment of inventive step?

answer justification: According to the text, prior art means publicly available art at the priority date, and not some internal prior art known only within the company employing the inventors. question_text: Which of the following statements is true about the skilled person under Article 56 EPC?

answer_choices.d: The skilled person under Article 56 EPC is the person who has the teaching of specialist documents.

answer justification: According to the text, the skilled person under Article 56 EPC is the person qualified to solve the established objective technical problem.

question_text: In the context of mixed-type inventions, which of the following is a legitimate way to formulate the technical problem to be solved in order to avoid taking into account a non-technical contribution when assessing inventive step?

answer_choices.a: Formulating the technical problem to contain pointers to the solution or partially anticipate it.
answer_choices.b: Excluding any feature that appears in the claim from the formulation of the problem.
answer_choices.c: Including an aim to be achieved in a non-technical field as part of the framework of the technical problem to be solved.
answer_choices.d: Formulating the technical problem in such a way that "there is a possibility of an inventive step being involved by purely non-technical features".

answer justification: According to the text, the board in T 641/00 allowed an aim to be achieved in a non-technical field to appear in the formulation of the problem as part of the framework of the technical problem that is to be solved, in order to avoid taking into account a non-technical contribution when assessing inventive step.

question_text: Which of the following is the correct interpretation of the term "technical" with respect to computer programs according to the jurisprudence of the boards of appeal?

answer_choices.a: Any technical considerations are sufficient to confer technical character on claimed subject matter.
answer_choices.b: Technical considerations aiming to solve problems "merely" relating to programming such as maintainability, re-usability and understandability of program code can confer technical character on claimed subject matter.
answer_choices.c: Technical considerations aiming to solve problems "merely" relating to the presentation of information can confer technical character on claimed subject matter.
answer_choices.d: Technical considerations aiming to solve problems "merely" relating to the physical interactions between program (software) and computer (hardware) can confer technical character on claimed subject matter.

question_text: Which of the following is a non-technical aim according to the board in T 1834/10?

answer_choices.a: The desire to present a selection of images
answer_choices.b: The desire to limit the selection to a predetermined number of images
answer_choices.c: The desire to present the selected images in some preferred layout
answer_choices.d: The desire to present the meaning of the display data

answer justification: According to the text, the board in T 1834/10 considers the desire to present a selection of images, to limit the selection to a predetermined number of images, and to present the selected images in some preferred layout as non-technical aims. The meaning of the display data does not convey any technical character to the presentation.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for considering a mathematical algorithm to contribute to the technical character of an invention?

answer_choices.a: The algorithm is not a technical process.
answer_choices.b: The algorithm does not produce a direct technical result.
answer_choices.c: The algorithm is carried out on a physical entity.
answer_choices.d: The algorithm serves a technical purpose.

answer justification: According to the text, mathematical algorithms may contribute to the technical character of an invention only insofar as they serve a technical purpose. Therefore, option D is a reason for considering a mathematical algorithm to contribute to the technical character of an invention.

question_text: Which of the following is not a field of technology where a technical contribution was found in the case law?

answer_choices.a: Heartbeat monitoring method
answer_choices.b: Image processing
answer_choices.c: Live web applications ranking
answer_choices.d: Vehicle navigation system

answer justification: According to the text, in T 598/07, T 1286/09, and T 1510/10, a technical contribution was found in the fields of heartbeat monitoring method, image processing, and live web applications ranking. However, in T 505/18, the board recognized improved safety in the technical context of the invention, which was real-time route guidance of a driver of a vehicle, as being a technical effect. Therefore, option D is not a field of technology where a technical contribution was found in the case law.
source: The case law mentioned in the text.

question_text: Which of the following is the correct statement about the game apparatus in the text?

answer_choices.a: The game rules are not meaningful only in a gaming context.
answer_choices.b: The game rules do not govern the conduct and actions of the players during game play.
answer_choices.c: The game rules do not have any further technical effects in the particular manner of technical implementation.
answer_choices.d: The game rules are not the direct technical consequence of the particular technical way selected data is used to determine a display state.

answer justification: According to the text, the board was unable to identify any further technical effects in the particular manner of technical implementation that might have rendered it non-obvious to the skilled person. This means that the game rules do not have any further technical effects in the particular manner of technical implementation.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for excluding a feature from being considered in the assessment of inventive step of a combination of features?

answer_choices.a: The feature contributes causally to the solution of the problem.
answer_choices.b: The feature is a technical non-functional modification.
answer_choices.c: The feature is not described in the description.
answer_choices.d: The feature does not provide a surprising advantage.

answer justification: According to the text, a feature is only to be considered in the assessment of inventive step if it contributes causally to the solution of the problem. Therefore, a feature that does not provide a surprising advantage is not a reason for excluding it from being considered. However, if a feature does not contribute causally to the solution of the problem, it is not relevant for the assessment of inventive step.
source: I.D.9. Assessment of inventive step, T 37/82, T 65/87, T 144/90, T 206/91, T 226/94, T 912/94

question_text: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the burden of proof when the credibility that a technical effect is achieved by substantially all claimed compounds is at issue?

answer_choices.a: The opponent has the burden of proving that the effect is not achieved.
answer_choices.b: The patentee has the burden of proving that the effect is achieved.
answer_choices.c: The burden of proof is shared between the patentee and the opponent.
answer_choices.d: The burden of proof is not relevant in this case.

answer justification: According to the text, when the credibility that a technical effect is achieved by substantially all claimed compounds is at issue and in a situation where it is prima facie unlikely that this is credible, it is not the opponent, but the patentee who has the burden of proving that the effect is achieved.

question_text: Which of the following is not a reason for a step to be considered obvious in the context of inventive step?

answer_choices.a: The step is a natural choice of a material generally available on the market and suitable for the purpose.
answer_choices.b: The step is a normal aim of the skilled person.
answer_choices.c: The step is a result of automation.
answer_choices.d: The step is a result of routine experimentation.

answer justification: According to the text, a step that is a result of routine experimentation is not considered obvious in the context of inventive step.

question_text: Which of the following is a secondary indication of inventive step?

answer_choices.a: The satisfaction of a long-felt need
answer_choices.b: The overcoming of a prejudice in the professional world
answer_choices.c: Economic success
answer_choices.d: The lack of a technical prejudice

answer justification: According to the text, secondary indicia such as the satisfaction of a long-felt need, the overcoming of a prejudice in the professional world, or economic success, are auxiliary considerations in assessing inventive step. Therefore, options A, B, and C are secondary indications of inventive step.

question_text: Which of the following is not a reason for considering commercial success as an indicator of inventive step?

answer_choices.a: Commercial success might have been due to factors other than its properties.
answer_choices.b: Commercial success alone can be regarded as forming the basis for an indication of inventive step.
answer_choices.c: Commercial success is not a factor that can be considered in the assessment of inventive step.
answer_choices.d: Commercial success must be demonstrated and it must be shown that such success resulted from the claimed invention and not from one or more other causes.

answer justification: According to the text, commercial success alone cannot be regarded as forming the basis for an indication of inventive step.

question_text: Which of the following is the correct interpretation of the term "industrial" in the context of Article 57 EPC 1973?

answer_choices.a: The term "industrial" in the context of Article 57 EPC 1973 refers to technical processes that occur in "industry" in the narrower sense of what in German would be called "Industrie".
answer_choices.b: The term "industrial" in the context of Article 57 EPC 1973 refers to commercial applications.

answer_choices.d: The term "industrial" in the context of Article 57 EPC 1973 refers to technical processes that occur in "industry" in the sense of "commercial" applications.

question_text: Which of the following is the basis for all the therapeutic indications of the claimed subject -matter in T 1452/06?

answer_choices.a: The predicted role of the purported serine protease activity of the polypeptide of sequence SEQ ID NO: 24 in the degradation of the extracellular matrix.

question_text: Which of the following is not a reason for a claim to lack clarity according to the text?

answer_choices.a: The exact distinctions which delimit the scope of protection cannot be learnt from them.
answer_choices.b: The claims per se are contradictory.
answer_choices.c: The claims are not clear in themselves when read by the person skilled in the art, without any reference to the content of the description.
answer_choices.d: The claims are not free of contradiction.

answer justification: According to the text, a claim lacks clarity if the exact distinctions which delimit the scope of protection cannot be learnt from them, if the claims per se are contradictory, if they are not clear in themselves when read by the person skilled in the art, without any reference to the content of the description. However, the text does not mention that the claims must be free of contradiction as a reason for a claim to lack clarity.

question_text: What is the essential feature of a diagnostic method within the meaning of Art. 52(4) EPC 1973?

answer_choices.a: The diagnosis as the deductive medical or veterinary decision phase
answer_choices.b: The features relating to the preceding steps which are constitutive for making the diagnosis
answer_choices.c: The features relating to the diagnosis for curative purposes
answer_choices.d: The features relating to the diagnosis for diagnostic purposes

question_text: What is the requirement for the method for measuring a parameter to appear in the claim according to the case law summarised in T 849/11?

answer_choices.a: The method must be clearly indicated in the claim.
answer_choices.b: The method must be known to the skilled person.
answer_choices.c: The method must be the same for all methodologies known in the relevant technical field.
answer_choices.d: The method must be described in the description according to R. 29(6) EPC 1973.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for a claim not being supported by the description according to the EPC?

answer_choices.a: The subject matter of the claim is not taken from the description.
answer_choices.b: The subject matter of the claim is not described as an essential feature of the invention in the description.
answer_choices.c: The subject matter of the claim is described as an essential feature of the invention in the description but not in the claims.
answer_choices.d: The subject matter of the claim is described as an essential feature of the invention in both the description and the claims.

answer justification: According to the text, a claim which does not include a feature described in the application (on the proper interpretation of the description) as an essential feature of the invention, and which is therefore inconsistent with the description, is not supported by the description for the purpose of Art. 84 EPC 1973. Therefore, option B is a reason for a claim not being supported by the description according to the EPC.

question_text: What is the correct interpretation of a claim according to the text?

answer_choices.a: The claim can extend to gene constructs which compose any DNA in addition to the GBSS gene fragments.
answer_choices.b: The claim is interpreted based on the purpose of introducing the GBSS DNA fragment into the potato cells and integrating it into the genome.
answer_choices.c: The claim can be interpreted in a way that contradicts its actual content.
answer_choices.d: Two methods having no technical bearing on each other can form a single multi-step process.

question_text: What is the effect of a change in the description or drawings of a patent on the understanding of a claimed feature?

answer_choices.a: It may have no influence on the understanding of a claimed feature
answer_choices.b: It may lead to a narrowing of the extent of the protection conferred

answer_choices.d: It may have no influence on the understanding of the patent as a whole

question_text: Which of the following is a requirement for a product-by-process claim to be valid under the EPC 1973?

answer_choices.a: The claim must define the product structurally.
answer_choices.b: The claim must mention all the specific conditions needed to obtain the products whose novelty can be demonstrated.
answer_choices.c: The claim must include all the process parameters required for unambiguously defining the claimed substances as inevitable process products.
answer_choices.d: The claim must indicate the method by which the reaction mixture is processed to obtain the claimed substances.

answer justification: According to the text, a product-by-process claim must include all the process parameters required for unambiguously defining the claimed substances as inevitable process products. This means that option C is a requirement for a product-by-process claim to be valid under the EPC 1973.

question_text: What is the requirement for a European patent application according to Article 82 EPC?

answer_choices.a: The application must relate to one invention only.
answer_choices.b: The application must relate to a group of inventions that are not linked.
answer_choices.c: The application must relate to a group of inventions that are not so linked as to form a single general inventive concept.
answer_choices.d: The application must relate to a group of inventions that are not so linked as to form a single general inventive concept and are not oriented towards the end products.

answer justification: According to the text, Article 82 EPC requires that the European patent application must relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept. Therefore, option C is the correct answer.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for considering two sets of intermediates as being technically sufficiently closely related by their contribution to an essential structural element of the end products?

answer_choices.a: The orientation of the intermediates towards the end products permits the individual technical problems addressed by the intermediates to be combined into a unitary overall problem to the solution of which both sets of purpose-made intermediates contribute.
answer_choices.b: The former are not even destroyed when the admixture is prepared and fully retain their properties and functions in the product, unlike typical intermediates, which lose their properties and functions when the admixture is prepared.
answer_choices.c: The intact components and the corresponding compositions in a mixture are technically interconnected by incorporation.
answer_choices.d: The intermediates are structurally related to each other.

answer justification: According to the text, the intact components and the corresponding compositions in a mixture are technically interconnected by incorporation. Therefore, option C is a reason for considering two sets of intermediates as being technically sufficiently closely related by their contribution to an essential structural element of the end products.

question_text: What is the common technical feature shared by all the processes claimed in the application described in T 957/96?

answer_choices.a: The use of a specific catalyst
answer_choices.b: The use of a specific solvent
answer_choices.c: The use of a specific temperature
answer_choices.d: The use of a substantially pure regioisomer

question_text: In T 2289/09, what was the Enlarged Board's statement regarding the invention which is to be examined in a divisional application?

answer_choices.a: The invention must be an invention in respect of which a search fee has been paid prior to the drawing up of the European search report.
answer_choices.b: The invention must be an invention in respect of which a search fee has been paid prior to the drawing up of the international search report.
answer_choices.c: The invention must be an invention in respect of which a search fee has been paid prior to the filing of the divisional application.
answer_choices.d: The invention must be an invention in respect of which a search fee has been paid prior to the filing of the parent application.

answer justification: According to the text, the Enlarged Board stated that "the invention which is to be examined ... must be an invention in respect of which a search fee has been paid prior to the drawing up of the European search report".

question_text: Which of the following is a source of information that the skilled person can use to supplement the information in the application and correct any errors identified in the assessment of sufficiency of disclosure under Article 83 EPC?

answer_choices.a: Secret know-how of individual makers of aerated concrete.
answer_choices.b: Textbooks or monographs.
answer_choices.c: The knowledge potentially available to any skilled person in the field.
answer_choices.d: The knowledge of a head of a laboratory.

answer justification: According to the text, the skilled person can supplement the information in the application with common general knowledge, which is the knowledge potentially available to any skilled person in the field. Therefore, option C is a source of information that the skilled person can use to supplement the information in the application and correct any errors identified in the assessment of sufficiency of disclosure under Article 83 EPC.

question_text: What is the minimum requirement for an invention to be considered sufficiently disclosed?

answer_choices.a: At least one way of carrying out the invention must be clearly indicated enabling the person skilled in the art to carry out the invention.
answer_choices.b: The invention must be described in mathematical terms.
answer_choices.c: The invention must be described in a way that is not subject to interpretation.
answer_choices.d: The invention must be described in a way that is not subject to debate.

answer justification: According to the text, an invention is in principle sufficiently disclosed if at least one way is clearly indicated enabling the person skilled in the art to carry out the invention. This means that the minimum requirement for an invention to be considered sufficiently disclosed is that at least one way of carrying out the invention must be clearly indicated.

question_text: In the context of patent law, which of the following is a correct statement about the sufficiency of disclosure of an invention?

answer_choices.a: If the skilled person, upon consideration of the entire disclosure and possibly using common general knowledge, could infer what would and what would not work, a claimed invention is sufficiently disclosed, even if a broad construction might also encompass what does not work.
answer_choices.b: If the quality of the coatings obtained does not meet the requirements set out in a claim, the invention is not sufficiently disclosed.
answer_choices.c: If the skilled person cannot directly recognise and exclude embodiments which obviously would not achieve the effect sought, the invention is not sufficiently disclosed.
answer_choices.d: If the invention does not solve the problem or achieve the desired effect, the invention is not sufficiently disclosed.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for a patent to be considered insufficiently disclosed?

answer_choices.a: The patent describes three clearly defined standard methods of determining a parameter.
answer_choices.b: The patent does not indicate any method for the measurement of a parameter.
answer_choices.c: The alleged ambiguity arises at the edges of the values recited in the claim.
answer_choices.d: The patent describes numerous methods of measuring a parameter.

answer justification: According to the text, if a patent does not indicate any method for the measurement of a parameter, it may be considered insufficiently disclosed.

question_text: Question 1: In the case of a patent relying on a newly formulated and unfamiliar parameter to define the solution of a technical problem, what is the patentee's particular obligation according to T 172/99?

answer_choices.a: To disclose all the information necessary to reliably define the new parameter in a formally correct and complete manner such that its values can be obtained by a person skilled in the art without undue burden.

answer_choices.c: To disclose all the information necessary to reliably define the new parameter in a manner which ensures that the claimed subject matter does not cover variants incapable of providing the relevant effect or solving the associated technical problem.
answer_choices.d: To disclose all the information necessary to reliably define the new parameter in a manner which ensures that the claimed subject matter covers only variants capable of providing the relevant effect or solving the associated technical problem.

question_text: Which of the following is a matter related to Art. 83 EPC?

answer_choices.a: The question of whether a skilled person is working or not within the claimed scope ("forbidden area" of a claim)
answer_choices.b: The definition of the scope of protection sought (Art. 84 EPC)
answer_choices.c: The question of whether a claimed essential parameter can be measured by the skilled person
answer_choices.d: The question of whether a claimed invention may be carried out with the aid of only a few additional non-disclosed steps

answer justification: According to the text, the question of whether a claimed essential parameter can be measured by the skilled person is related to Art. 83 EPC. This is because the sufficiency of disclosure requirement under Art. 83 EPC ensures that the skilled person can carry out the invention without having to do their own research or performing an unreasonable number of experiments. If the skilled person cannot measure the relevant essential parameter, they may have to perform their own research or experiments to determine the parameter, which would not meet the sufficiency of disclosure requirement.

question_text: What is the main reason why the board in T 2070/13 concluded that the skilled person was unable to identify suitable materials displaying anti-adherence?

answer_choices.a: The board did not find any suitable compounds within the claimed families of compounds.
answer_choices.b: The board did not find any standard procedure to determine anti-adherence.
answer_choices.c: The board found that the skilled person would be faced with an experimental programme to establish which of the listed materials satisfied the claimed criterion of anti-adherence.
answer_choices.d: The board found that the enhancers to be used were characterized in functional terms only.

answer justification: The board in T 2070/13 concluded that the skilled person was unable to identify suitable materials displaying anti-adherence due to the large number of potential materials listed, several of these listed materials also describing large families of compounds; the skilled person would be faced with an experimental programme in order to establish which of the listed materials satisfied the claimed criterion of anti-adherence.

question_text: Which of the following is a fundamental principle of patent law?

answer_choices.a: A claim can validly cover broad subject matter only if the description of the relevant patent enables every method of arriving at that subject matter to be carried out.
answer_choices.b: A claim can validly cover broad subject matter, even though the description of the relevant patent does not enable every method of arriving at that subject matter to be carried out.
answer_choices.c: A claim can only cover subject matter that is already known to the skilled person at the priority date.
answer_choices.d: A claim can only cover subject matter that is not anticipated in the prior art.

answer justification: According to the text, it is a fundamental principle of patent law that a claim can validly cover broad subject matter, even though the description of the relevant patent does not enable every method of arriving at that subject matter to be carried out. This is because if every method of arriving at the subject matter had to be enabled, no dominant patent could exist, and each developer of a new method of arriving at that subject matter would be free of earlier patents.

question_text: What is the main line of case law identified in T 116/18 regarding sufficiency of disclosure under Article 83 EPC?

answer_choices.c: "no plausibility"
answer_choices.d: "plausibility was ultimately established"

question_text: What is the requirement for inventions involving biological material which is not available to the public and cannot be described in the European patent application?

answer_choices.b: A deposit of the biological material with a recognised depositary institution is necessary.
answer_choices.c: The biological material must be described in the European patent application.
answer_choices.d: The biological material must be available to the public.

question_text: Which of the following is the correct statement about the clarity requirement of Article 83 EPC?

answer_choices.a: The clarity requirement of Article 83 EPC is not applicable if the wording of a claim is perfectly clear.
answer_choices.b: The clarity requirement of Article 83 EPC is not applicable if there is a discrepancy between the claims and the description.
answer_choices.c: The clarity requirement of Article 83 EPC is applicable if the expression used in the claim is very broad.
answer_choices.d: The clarity requirement of Article 83 EPC is applicable if the claim is not limited to a specific embodiment of the description.

answer justification: According to the text, when the wording of a claim is perfectly clear it needs to be considered under Article 83 EPC, rather than undertaking another speculative interpretation of the claim. Therefore, option A is the correct statement about the clarity requirement of Article 83 EPC.

question_text: What is the burden of proof for establishing sufficiency of disclosure when a weak presumption exists that the invention is sufficiently disclosed?

answer_choices.a: The burden of proof is on the patent proprietor.
answer_choices.b: The burden of proof is on the opponent.
answer_choices.c: The burden of proof is on the examining division.
answer_choices.d: The burden of proof is on the board of appeal.

question_text: The board in T 1273/09 had serious doubts that the claimed homeopathic treatment of hypertension could be reliably and reproducibly achieved by the mixture claimed for the following reasons:

answer_choices.b: The transfer of the priority right is governed by the law of the state where the first application was filed.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for the priority document to disclose the broad group of activators functionally defined in claim 1 of the European patent?

answer_choices.b: The priority document did not mention any activator.

answer_choices.d: The priority document mentioned activators that comply with the functional definition in the European patent but not in the broad group defined in claim 1.

question_text: Which of the following is a requirement for claiming priority in a subsequent application?

answer_choices.a: The features of the invention disclosed in the priority application must not characterise the invention claimed in the subsequent application.
answer_choices.b: The features of the invention disclosed in the priority application must characterise the invention claimed in the subsequent application.

answer_choices.d: The features of the invention disclosed in the priority application are not relevant for claiming priority in a subsequent application.

question_text: Which of the following is a requirement for an application to be considered as the first application by the applicant or by his predecessor in title in respect of the invention?

answer_choices.a: The application must be filed by the inventor.
answer_choices.b: The application must be filed by the applicant or his predecessor in title.
answer_choices.c: The application must be filed by a legal entity.
answer_choices.d: The application must be filed by a person who is economically independent of the applicant.

answer justification: According to the text, an application giving rise to the priority right had to be the first application by the applicant or by his predecessor in title in respect of the invention.
