answer_choices.b: The proposed amendments were judged as inadmissible by the board of appeal, but the legal consequence of this was that they were never integrated into the text of the application and never became part of it.
answer_choices.c: The proposed amendments were judged as inadmissible by the board of appeal, but the legal consequence of this was that they were integrated into the text of the application and became part of it.
answer_choices.d: The proposed amendments were judged as admissible by the board of appeal, but the legal consequence of this was that they were never integrated into the text of the application and never became part of it.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for postponing oral proceedings according to the EPC?

answer_choices.a: The desire of a party to be present at oral proceedings
answer_choices.b: Flight cancellation along with impossibility of using other travel means
answer_choices.c: Late receipt of board's communication
answer_choices.d: Attendance of one of the inventors is relevant for the discussion of formal and substantive points in the oral proceedings

answer justification: According to the text, in T 174/16, the board held that it was unreasonable to consider a flight cancellation, along with the impossibility of using other travel means, not to constitute "serious reasons" within the meaning of the relevant provisions. Therefore, flight cancellation along with impossibility of using other travel means is a reason for postponing oral proceedings according to the EPC.

question_text: What is the main concern for refusing material filed after the final date set under R. 71a EPC 1973 in opposition proceedings?

answer_choices.a: The examining division has its own technical expertise and does not need to consult clients and technical experts.
answer_choices.b: The applicant's interest in obtaining proper patent protection for his claimed invention is not important.
answer_choices.c: The EPO's interest in bringing the examination procedure to a speedy close by the issue of a decision is not important.
answer_choices.d: Parties to opposition proceedings are not often represented by professional representatives.

answer justification: According to the text, the main concern for refusing material filed after the final date set under R. 71a EPC 1973 in opposition proceedings is that parties to opposition proceedings are often represented by professional representatives, who would need to consult their clients and technical experts for further instructions to deal with new requests or evidence. This means that option D is not correct.

question_text: What is the practice of the board regarding handwritten amendments to patent documents during oral proceedings?

answer_choices.a: The board allows handwritten amendments to patent documents during oral proceedings.
answer_choices.b: The board does not allow handwritten amendments to patent documents during oral proceedings.
answer_choices.c: The board allows handwritten amendments to patent documents during oral proceedings, but only if it is not detrimental to the principles of due process and procedural economy.
answer_choices.d: The board does not have a practice regarding handwritten amendments to patent documents during oral proceedings.

question_text: Who is allowed to attend the deliberations of the board according to Art. 19(1), second sentence, RPBA 2020?

answer_choices.a: Only members of the board
answer_choices.b: The chairman may authorise other officers to attend
answer_choices.c: The chairman may authorise other parties to attend
answer_choices.d: The chairman may authorise other employees to attend

question_text: Which of the following is the correct interpretation of the term "general dislocation" as used in Rule 134(2) EPC?

answer_choices.a: A disruption caused by a specific event such as the COVID-19 outbreak
answer_choices.b: A disruption caused by any event that affects the EPO's ability to function
answer_choices.c: A disruption caused by a decision of a department of first instance or a board of appeal
answer_choices.d: A disruption caused by a statutory period

answer justification: According to the text, the term "general dislocation" refers to interruptions that affect the EPO's ability to function, regardless of the cause. Therefore, option B is the correct interpretation of the term "general dislocation" as used in Rule 134(2) EPC.
source: Article III.D.1 of the law text.

question_text: What is the standard for determining legal incapacity of a representative for the purpose of Rule 142(1)(c) EPC?

answer_choices.a: The standard is determined by the relevant national law.
answer_choices.b: The standard is determined by the EPO.
answer_choices.c: depending on the nationality or domicile of the representative. Therefore, option D is the correct answer.
answer_choices.d: The standard is determined by a uniform standard of judging legal incapacity.

answer justification: According to the text, a uniform standard of judging legal incapacity shall apply in order to avoid differences in the application of R. 90(1)(c) EPC 1973 (R. 142(1)(c) EPC) depending on the nationality or domicile of the representative. Therefore, option D is the correct answer.

question_text: Which of the following is a time limit for which it is for the applicant to observe under Article 122(1) EPC?

answer_choices.a: The time limit for filing a statement of grounds of appeal under Article 108, third sentence, EPC
answer_choices.b: The time limit for filing the notice of opposition and paying the appropriate fee under Article 99(1) EPC
answer_choices.c: The time limit for forwarding a European patent application filed with a national office to the EPO in time
answer_choices.d: The time limit for paying renewal fees which had fallen due during the period of the representative's or applicant's incapacity

question_text: Is the requirement of pendency when filing a divisional application a time limit?

answer_choices.a: Yes
answer_choices.b: No

source: Article 36(1) EPC and Article 25(1) EPC 1973 in its version since 2002.

question_text: In which of the following cases was the removal of the cause of non-compliance with the two-month time limit of R. 136(1) EPC not the date on which the applicant had inspected the file and realised that its former representative had not acted properly?

answer_choices.d: None of the above

question_text: What is a prerequisite for granting re-establishment of rights due to financial difficulties?

answer_choices.a: The financial difficulties were not due to circumstances beyond the reasonable control of the applicant.
answer_choices.b: The applicant did not try with all due care to obtain financial support.
answer_choices.c: The financial difficulties were not experienced through no fault of one's own.
answer_choices.d: The applicant did not file the request for re-establishment of rights in due time.

answer justification: According to the text, financial difficulties experienced through no fault of one's own and leading to failure to observe time limits for the payment of fees can constitute grounds for granting re-establishment of rights. Therefore, option C is a prerequisite for granting re-establishment of rights due to financial difficulties.

question_text: What is the requirement for a system for monitoring time limits in general according to T 428/98 and T 1465/07?

answer_choices.a: The system should not incorporate an overall checking mechanism which is independent of the person responsible for monitoring time limits.
answer_choices.b: The system should not make sure that monitoring duties are not left to one person alone.
answer_choices.c: The system should not involve a second system for monitoring time limits, the latter has to be independent of the former ("redundant").
answer_choices.d: The system should not be organised more economically than in a smaller one.

answer justification: According to the text, the requirements to be met by a system for monitoring time limits in general include making sure that monitoring duties are not left to one person alone, and that the system incorporates an overall checking mechanism which is independent of the person responsible for monitoring time limits. This checking mechanism can be provided within a single system for monitoring time limits. If the checking mechanism involves a second system for monitoring time limits, the latter has to be independent of the former ("redundant").

question_text: In which of the following situations can an applicant rely on its professional representative to deal with the EPO?

answer_choices.a: When the applicant is on notice that a time limit has not been met and/or that instructions are required in order to meet it.
answer_choices.b: When the applicant has issued a "stop work" order to its US representative.
answer_choices.c: When the former representative has not been capable of running the case in a proper way due to health reasons beyond his control.
answer_choices.d: When the applicant has no reason to suspect that the representative can be relied on.

answer justification: According to the text, in the case where the former representative has not been capable of running the case in a proper way due to health reasons beyond his control, the applicant can rely on its professional representative to deal with the EPO.
source: III.E.5. Merit of request for re -establishment of rights, T 381/93 of 12 August 1994.

question_text: In which of the following cases was the misinterpretation of a provision of the EPC by a representative not without basis or unreasonable?
answer justification: In J 28/92, the Legal Board held that the misinterpretation of a provision of the EPC by a representative was not without basis or unreasonable, considering that there was no basis for penalising the representative for having arrived at a not unreasonable interpretation of a rule of the EPC, which subsequently turned out to be wrong.

question_text: Which of the following tasks can a representative entrust to an assistant without infringing all due care in dealing with the filing of the grounds of appeal?

answer_choices.a: Sending the statement of grounds of appeal to the EPO by fax on the final date of the relevant time limit
answer_choices.b: Writing the statement of grounds of appeal
answer_choices.c: Supervising the assistant who is writing the statement of grounds of appeal
answer_choices.d: Checking whether the fax has actually been despatched after the assistant has sent it

answer justification: According to the text, in a properly organised office, the representative can rely on the correct execution of a task like sending a letter or a fax prepared and signed by the representative. This means that the representative can entrust this task to an assistant without infringing all due care in dealing with the filing of the grounds of appeal.
source: Article III.E.5. Merit of request for re -establishment of rights.

question_text: Which department is competent to decide on the request for re-establishment of rights in respect of the time limit for filing a notice of appeal?

answer_choices.a: The department competent to decide on the omitted act
answer_choices.b: The department competent to decide whether the appeal was inadmissible for non-compliance with Article 108 EPC
answer_choices.c: The department competent to decide on the request for re-establishment in respect of any time limit
answer_choices.d: The department competent to decide on the request for re-establishment in respect of the time limit for filing a statement of grounds of appeal

answer justification: According to the text, the department competent to decide on the request for re-establishment in respect of the time limit for filing a notice of appeal is the department competent to decide whether the appeal was inadmissible for non-compliance with Article 108 EPC, which is under R. 101(1) EPC the board of appeal.

question_text: Which of the following statements best describes the principle of proportionality as it is used in the case law of the Boards of Appeal of the European Patent Office?

answer_choices.a: The principle of proportionality is a main ground for assessing the allowability of an appeal.
answer_choices.b: The principle of proportionality is a duty for a court or an administration to find a balance between a party's error and the legally ensuing consequences when a margin of weighing the importance of the circumstances exists.
answer_choices.c: The principle of proportionality is never used as a main ground but only in support of other grounds already substantiating the allowability of an appeal.
answer_choices.d: The principle of proportionality is a duty for a court or an administration to find a balance between a party's error and the legally ensuing consequences when a margin of weighing the importance of the circumstances does not exist.

answer justification: According to the text, the principle of proportionality is never used as a main ground but only in support of other grounds already substantiating the allowability of an appeal.

question_text: Which of the following is true about the use of an alternative official language in appeal proceedings under R. 2(1) EPC 1973?

answer_choices.a: Appeal proceedings are a mere continuation of first-instance proceedings.
answer_choices.b: A party can choose to use one of the official languages set out in Art. 14(1) EPC 1973.
answer_choices.c: A party has a right to both speak and hear in the language it chooses, as long as the conditions of R. 2(1) EPC 1973 are fulfilled.
answer_choices.d: A party can use the other official language already used by it in the oral proceedings before the opposition division, without fulfilling the requirements of R. 2(1) EPC 1973 as they apply to the pending appeal proceedings.

question_text: What is the language to be used for taking evidence and writing the minutes according to the EPC?

answer_choices.a: The language of the proceedings
answer_choices.b: The language of the country where the evidence is taken
answer_choices.c: The language of the witness
answer_choices.d: The language of the party requesting the evidence

answer justification: According to the text, the language to be used for taking evidence and writing the minutes is governed by Art. 14(3) EPC (language of the proceedings) and R. 4 EPC (derogations from the provisions on use of the language of the proceedings in oral proceedings).

question_text: What is the difference between a witness and an expert according to the boards of appeal?

answer_choices.a: A witness is put forward to substantiate facts of which he/she has personal knowledge, while an expert is put forward to provide an opinion on a technical matter.
answer_choices.b: A witness is put forward to provide an opinion on a technical matter, while an expert is put forward to substantiate facts of which he/she has personal knowledge.
answer_choices.c: A witness is put forward to provide an opinion on a legal matter, while an expert is put forward to substantiate facts of which he/she has personal knowledge.
answer_choices.d: A witness is put forward to substantiate facts of which he/she has personal knowledge, while an expert is put forward to provide an opinion on a legal matter.

answer justification: According to the text, a witness is put forward to substantiate facts of which he/she has personal knowledge, while an expert is put forward to provide an opinion on a technical matter.
source: Article III.G.2. Admissible evidence 813 f) of the EPC.

question_text: What is the effect of a party not objecting to the accuracy of the minutes of the oral proceedings as evidence of the course of the proceedings?

answer_choices.a: The minutes are not considered a faithful account of events.
answer_choices.b: The minutes are considered a faithful account of events but can be disregarded.
answer_choices.c: The minutes are considered a faithful account of events and are admitted as evidence.
answer_choices.d: The minutes are not considered a faithful account of events and are not admitted as evidence.

answer justification: According to the text, in various cases concerning prior use, the minutes of the oral proceedings have never been challenged. Since the minutes are not disputed, they are considered a faithful account of events and are admitted as evidence.
source: Law of evidence 818, T 361/00, T 2301/12, R 6/17.

question_text: Which of the following is not a reason for the examining division to reject evidence as late-filed in ex parte case T 545/08?

answer_choices.a: The division had cited document D1 at the beginning of the examination proceedings.
answer_choices.b: The division had provided no further explanations or evidence as to the document's public availability before the priority date.
answer_choices.c: The division had not properly raised the objections based on this document.
answer_choices.d: The division had provided persuasive arguments for the exercise of its discretion.

answer justification: According to the text, the examining division should not have rejected the appellant's further evidence as late-filed in ex parte case T 545/08 because it had not provided persuasive arguments for the exercise of its discretion. Therefore, option D is not a reason for the examining division to reject evidence as late-filed in this case.

question_text: When should evidence that the requirements for a stay of the proceedings as per R. 14(1) EPC had been met be provided?

answer_choices.a: After the mention of the grant of the patent
answer_choices.b: During the oral proceedings before the board
answer_choices.c: Before the mention of the grant of the patent
answer_choices.d: After the mention of the opposition

answer justification: According to the text, evidence that the requirements for a stay of the proceedings as per R. 14(1) EPC had to be provided while the proceedings for grant were still pending and thus before the mention of the grant was published in the European Patent Bulletin. Any evidence not submitted by then should not be taken into account by the EPO.

question_text: Which of the following is true about third-party observations in patent proceedings under the EPC?

answer_choices.a: Third-party observations can be considered at first instance and on appeal, but there is no obligation on the board beyond such consideration.
answer_choices.b: Third parties have the same procedural rights as parties to the proceedings, including the right to be heard.
answer_choices.c: Parties to the proceedings can comment at any stage on new facts and evidence emerging from third-party observations filed after the opposition period.
answer_choices.d: Third parties have the right to be heard in patent proceedings under the EPC.

answer justification: According to the text, third-party observations can be considered at first instance and on appeal, but there is no obligation on the board beyond such consideration. Therefore, option A is the correct answer.
source: Article 117(1) and Article 113(1) EPC, T 390/07, T 1756/11, G 4/92.

question_text: Which of the following is a shortcoming that can lead a board of appeal to overrule the evaluation of evidence made by a department of first instance?

answer_choices.a: Essential points had not been considered
answer_choices.b: Irrelevant matters had been taken into consideration
answer_choices.c: The laws of thought had not been violated
answer_choices.d: The board of appeal disagrees with the evaluation of evidence made by the department of first instance

answer justification: According to the text, a board of appeal can overrule the evaluation of evidence made by a department of first instance if essential points had not been considered. This is one of the shortcomings mentioned in the text that can lead a board of appeal to overrule the evaluation of evidence made by a department of first instance.

question_text: In which of the following situations would the comparative tests provided sufficient evidence that the problem was solved?

answer_choices.a: The comparative tests were made with one specific printer on one specific paper, both different from the paper and the printer used in example 18 of the closest state of the art.
answer_choices.b: The comparative tests were made with the same printer and the same paper as the closest state of the art.
answer_choices.c: The comparative tests were made with one specific printer on one specific paper, both the same as the paper and the printer used in example 18 of the closest state of the art.
answer_choices.d: The comparative tests were made with a different printer and a different paper than the closest state of the art, but the results were not convincingly shown to have their origin in the distinguishing feature of the invention.

question_text: Which of the following is the standard of proof generally applied by the EPO departments?

answer_choices.a: The balance of probabilities
answer_choices.b: Beyond reasonable doubt
answer_choices.c: Absolute conviction
answer_choices.d: Up to the hilt

answer justification: According to the text, the EPO standard of proof is generally the balance of probabilities. Therefore, option A is the correct answer.
source: Law of evidence 848, 4.3, General – "Balance of probabilities".

question_text: Which of the following is the correct standard of proof for a public prior use allegation when the evidence lies within the power and knowledge of the opponent?

answer_choices.a: The balance of probabilities
answer_choices.b: Beyond all reasonable doubt
answer_choices.c: The overall balance of probabilities
answer_choices.d: The standard of proof "beyond any reasonable doubt"

answer justification: According to the text, the stricter standard of proof "beyond all reasonable doubt" has been used, exceptionally, in cases of public prior use where all the supporting evidence lay within the power and knowledge of the opponent.

question_text: In the context of the public availability of commercial brochures, which of the following standards of proof is considered appropriate by the board in T 1140/09?

answer_choices.a: The balance of probabilities
answer_choices.b: Up to the hilt
answer_choices.c: Beyond reasonable doubt
answer_choices.d: Strict scrutiny

answer justification: In T 1140/09, the board considered the "balance of probabilities" to be the proper standard of proof to be applied for the question of the public availability of document E3, a brochure that had been distributed by the appellant (opponent) to visitors at CeBIT and had therefore been made available to the public before the priority date.

question_text: Who bears the burden of proving receipt of documents by the EPO?

answer_choices.a: The patentee
answer_choices.b: The opponent
answer_choices.c: The EPO
answer_choices.d: The board of appeal

answer justification: According to the text, the respondent (opponent) bears the burden of proving receipt of documents by the EPO.

question_text: In T 862/11, which of the following is true?

answer_choices.a: The appellant (opponent) submitted comparative tests in support of its own assertion.
answer_choices.b: The appellant (opponent) failed to submit any evidence that an improvement was implausible.
answer_choices.c: The board regarded the problem as not solved.
answer_choices.d: The board did not regard the problem as solved.

answer justification: According to the text, in T 862/11, the appellant (opponent) failed to submit comparative tests in support of its own assertion that an improvement was implausible owing to the lack of any evidence.

question_text: Which of the following is the burden of proof for a party submitting that something has not happened?

answer_choices.a: The party can essentially presume what could have happened or what normally would have been done if a letter had been received, in order to cast doubt upon the EPO's evidence.
answer_choices.b: The EPO is also in a difficult situation if an applicant submits that it has not received a communication. The EPO then has to start enquiries with the postal services and rely on the information obtained.
answer_choices.c: The EPO must in a case of doubt ("im Zweifel") establish the date on which the letter was delivered.
answer_choices.d: The party can file compelling evidence that the letter was not received.

question_text: In a patent case, which of the following is true regarding the burden of proof for inventive step when there are contradictory test results?

answer_choices.a: The patent proprietor has the burden of proof to eliminate doubts on the effect allegedly achieved by the present invention.
answer_choices.b: The opponents have the burden of proof to demonstrate that the technical problem in question has not been solved.
answer_choices.c: The board has the burden of proof to determine whether the subject-matter of the claim solves the problem.
answer_choices.d: The patent proprietor has the burden of proof to demonstrate that the technical problem in question has been solved.

answer justification: According to the text, in T 570/08, the patent proprietor could not convincingly eliminate doubts on the effect allegedly achieved by the present invention, and the patent was revoked. This means that the patent proprietor has the burden of proof to eliminate doubts on the effect allegedly achieved by the present invention.

question_text: Which of the following is the correct order of the principles of interpretation of the Vienna Convention?

answer_choices.a: Literal interpretation, Systematic interpretation, Teleological interpretation, Subsequent agreement or practice, Secondary considerations: dynamic interpretation
answer_choices.b: Literal interpretation, Systematic interpretation, Teleological interpretation, Secondary considerations: dynamic interpretation, Subsequent agreement or practice
answer_choices.c: Systematic interpretation, Literal interpretation, Teleological interpretation, Subsequent agreement or practice, Secondary considerations: dynamic interpretation
answer_choices.d: Systematic interpretation, Literal interpretation, Teleological interpretation, Secondary considerations: dynamic interpretation, Subsequent agreement or practice

answer justification: According to the text, the principles of interpretation of the Vienna Convention are listed in the order of Literal interpretation, Systematic interpretation, Teleological interpretation, Subsequent agreement or practice, and Secondary considerations: dynamic interpretation.
source: III.H Interpretation of the EPC, 1.1.2 Supplementary means of interpretation – "travaux préparatoires".

question_text: Which of the following is the principle that the Enlarged Board of Appeal of the European Patent Office (EPO) does not apply without exception?

answer_choices.a: The principle of narrow construction of exceptions from patentability
answer_choices.b: The principle of broad construction of exceptions from patentability
answer_choices.c: The principle of literal interpretation of provisions of the EPC
answer_choices.d: The principle of contextual interpretation of provisions of the EPC

answer justification: According to the text, the Enlarged Board of Appeal of the EPO stated that the "frequently cited principle", according to which exclusion clauses from patentability laid down in the EPC are to be construed in a restrictive manner, does not apply without exception. Therefore, option A is the principle that the Enlarged Board of Appeal of the EPO does not apply without exception.

question_text: Which of the following is true about the relationship between TRIPS and the EPC?

answer_choices.a: TRIPS provisions are binding on the boards of appeal.
answer_choices.b: TRIPS provisions are not binding on the boards of appeal but can be used to interpret provisions of the EPC.
answer_choices.c: TRIPS provisions are binding on the legislator of the EPC.
answer_choices.d: TRIPS provisions are not relevant to the EPC.

answer justification: According to the text, TRIPS provisions are elements to be taken into consideration by the boards of appeal but are not binding on them. They can be used as a means to interpret provisions of the EPC.

question_text: Which of the following is not a correct statement about the power of the Council to lay down provisions concerning substantive law in the Implementing Regulations?

answer_choices.a: The Council is entitled to provide for issues of substantive law in the Rules of the Implementing Regulations.
answer_choices.b: A Rule must be clear enough to indicate to those applying it in what way the legislator intended the Article to be interpreted by means of that Rule.
answer_choices.c: The Council is competent to amend the Convention by amendment of the Implementing Regulations.
answer_choices.d: The Administrative Council is not competent to amend the Convention, here Art. 53(b)  EPC, by amendment of the Implementing Regulations.

answer justification: According to the text, the Administrative Council is not competent to amend the Convention, here Art. 53(b)  EPC, by amendment of the Implementing Regulations.
source: Article 164(2) EPC and Article 33(1)(b) and 35(3) EPC.

question_text: Which of the following is not a board's duty in relation to requests of equal ranking?

answer_choices.a: To give a legal opinion on the admissibility of several requests as guidance for appellants in defining the order in which they would like their requests to be examined.
answer_choices.b: To consider as inadmissible the appellant's request at the end of the oral proceedings that, should the outcome of the discussions be negative for him, he be given the opportunity to formulate new requests.
answer_choices.c: To give reasons for the rejection of each request in a decision.
answer_choices.d: To admit late-filed requests in appeal proceedings.

answer justification: According to the text, it is not the board's duty to give a legal opinion on the admissibility of several requests as guidance for appellants in defining the order in which they would like their requests to be examined.
source: III.I.4. Obligation to give reasons for refusal of each request, 903 3.2. Requests of equal ranking, T 148/06.

question_text: What is the principle that parties have a right to have their case decided by?

answer_choices.a: The principle that parties have a right to have their case decided by the judge appointed by law
answer_choices.b: The principle that parties have a right to have their case decided by the judge appointed by the board
answer_choices.c: The principle that parties have a right to have their case decided by the judge appointed by the Enlarged Board
answer_choices.d: The principle that parties have a right to have their case decided by the judge appointed by the European Court of Human Rights

answer justification: According to the text, parties have a right to have their case decided by the judge designated or appointed by law. This principle is even enshrined at a constitutional level in some EPC contracting states.

question_text: Which of the following is a sufficient proof of personal interest within the meaning of Article 24(1) EPC 1973?

answer_choices.a: A member of an opposition division was previously employed by a company dependent on a party to the opposition proceedings.
answer_choices.b: A member of an opposition division was previously employed by a company that is a competitor of a party to the opposition proceedings.

answer_choices.d: A member of an opposition division was previously employed by a company that is a customer of a party to the opposition proceedings.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for exclusion or objection of a board member under Article 3(2) RPBA 2020?

answer_choices.a: The board member has not provided details on whether they have deputised for the Vice-President of the EPO Directorate-General 3 (VP3).
answer_choices.b: The board member has not taken discretionary procedural steps which might disadvantage a particular party.
answer_choices.c: The board member has not admitted amended claims, regardless of whether the board had correctly used its power or discretion to do so.
answer_choices.d: The board member has not interpreted the steps taken as expressing bias against a particular party.

question_text: What is the correct statement about a former member of the boards of appeal sitting beside and assisting the respondent's representative during oral proceedings before the opposition division?

answer_choices.a: This is not allowed under the EPC.
answer_choices.b: This is allowed, but the former member cannot make any intervention of his own motion.
answer_choices.c: This is allowed, and the former member can make any intervention of his own motion.
answer_choices.d: This is allowed, and the former member can present his case before his former colleagues.

source: III.K.1.3.2. Formal aspects of decisions of EPO departments.

answer_choices.b: A number of procedural irregularities had occurred after the oral proceedings
answer_choices.c: If only one examiner took part in the prior proceedings, that examiner may not be chairman in the subsequent opposition proceedings under Art. 19(2) EPC
answer_choices.d: A change of the opposition division between the oral and written decision

answer justification: According to the text, an improper composition of the opposition division is a substantial procedural violation. question_text: Which of the following is a requirement for EPO decisions according to R. 113 EPC?

answer_choices.a: Decisions must be signed by the employee responsible.
answer_choices.b: Decisions must be signed by the employee responsible and state their name.
answer_choices.c: Decisions must be signed by the employee responsible and bear the seal of the EPO.
answer_choices.d: Decisions must be signed by the employee responsible, state their name, bear the seal of the EPO and be signed by all the division's members.

answer justification: According to the text, R. 113 EPC requires that decisions from the European Patent Office must be signed by the employee responsible.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for a decision to be considered insufficiently reasoned within the meaning of Rule 111(2) EPC?

answer_choices.a: The decision contains a summary of a party's submissions.
answer_choices.b: The decision does not deal with crucial counter-arguments presented by the applicant.
answer_choices.c: The decision merely states that no convincing arguments have been found in the letter.

answer_choices.d: The board's preliminary opinion in the communication under Article 15(1) RPBA 2020 was changed in the light of the oral discussion of arguments that were all already known from the written proceedings.

question_text: Which of the following is not a reason for the board to consider belated submissions as not justified in T 1904/16?

answer_choices.a: The submissions were not justified by the change of representative shortly before the oral proceedings.
answer_choices.b: The submissions were not justified by the change of the law.
answer_choices.c: The submissions were not justified by the change of the facts.
answer_choices.d: The submissions were not justified by the change of the opponent.

answer justification: According to the text, the board considered that the change of representative was not a reason for the board to consider belated submissions as justified. The change of the law, however, is not mentioned as a reason in this case.
source: V.A.4. New submissions on appeal – case law on the RPBA 2020.

question_text: What is the criterion that the boards consider even though it is not referred to in Art. 13(1) RPBA 2020, and cannot be decisive in view of the stage reached in the proceedings and the fact that the new submissions had not been occasioned by any statements made by the patent proprietor in the proceedings before the board or by the board itself?

answer_choices.a: Prima facie relevance
answer_choices.b: Prima facie irrelevance
answer_choices.c: Prima facie admissibility
answer_choices.d: Prima facie inadmissibility

answer justification: According to the text, the criterion of prima facie relevance is considered by the boards, even though it is not referred to in Art. 13(1) RPBA 2020. However, it cannot be decisive in view of the stage reached in the proceedings and the fact that the new submissions had not been occasioned by any statements made by the patent proprietor in the proceedings before the board or by the board itself.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for not admitting new requests at a very late procedural stage (shortly before the oral proceedings)?

answer_choices.a: The requests are prima facie allowable.
answer_choices.b: The requests are unsuitable from the outset to overcome the doubts as to the allowability of the claim.
answer_choices.c: The requests are filed very late (i.e. shortly before or during the oral proceedings).
answer_choices.d: The requests are not accompanied by reasons explaining why the amendments have been made and how they are intended to overcome the objections raised in the course of the proceedings.

answer justification: According to the text, the admission of new requests at a very late procedural stage (shortly before the oral proceedings) is only in keeping with the principle of procedural economy if the requests are not unsuitable from the outset to overcome the doubts as to the allowability of the claim. Therefore, the fact that the requests are filed very late (i.e. shortly before or during the oral proceedings) is a reason for not admitting them.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for refusing to admit new requests filed by the patentee in oral proceedings in appeal proceedings?

answer_choices.a: The subject of the proceedings has changed.
answer_choices.b: The patentee has repeatedly modified its requests until an acceptable set of claims is found.
answer_choices.c: The patentee has taken care not to act in a manner detrimental to the efficient conduct of oral proceedings.
answer_choices.d: The patentee has submitted requests willy -nilly, withdrawn them and then resubmitted them later.

answer justification: According to the text, the board in T 1790/06 took account of the conduct of the respondent (patentee) during the oral proceedings. A party's obligations included taking care not to act in a manner detrimental to the efficient conduct of oral proceedings. Submitting requests willy -nilly, withdrawing them and then resubmitting them later was unacceptable, for both the board and other parties. Therefore, option D is a reason for refusing to admit new requests filed by the patentee in oral proceedings in appeal proceedings.

question_text: In which of the following situations is it possible to file a new request after the debate has been closed during oral proceedings?

answer_choices.a: The new request is filed before the board announces its decision, and there is a justification for filing it so late.
answer_choices.b: The new request is filed after the board announces its decision, and there is a justification for filing it so late.
answer_choices.c: The new request is filed after the board announces its decision, and there is no justification for filing it so late.
answer_choices.d: The new request is filed before the board announces its decision, and there is no justification for filing it so late.

answer justification: According to the text, in T 360/13, the appellant filed a new request after the debate had been closed, but before the board announced its decision. The board noted that, once the debate had been closed, the criteria for admitting new submissions were especially strict. However, in this case, there was a justification for filing the new request so late. Therefore, option A is the correct answer.

question_text: What is the correct interpretation of the term "poly" -olefin" in the passage concerned in the application as filed?

answer_choices.b: "Polyolefin"

answer_choices.b: The request contains product and use claims which relate to fundamentally different subject matter.

answer_choices.d: The request could have been filed in the first-instance proceedings.

Therefore, if a request could have been filed in the first-instance proceedings, it is not admissible in appeal proceedings.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for not admitting new requests for reasons of procedural economy, even where not filed until a very late stage?

answer_choices.a: The amendments are justified, e.g. where filed in response to objections or comments which were not part of the decision under appeal but were raised in writing during the appeal proceedings.
answer_choices.b: The amendments extend the scope of discussion as determined by the decision under appeal and the statement of grounds of appeal.
answer_choices.c: The amendments do not introduce new objections under the EPC and overcome all outstanding objections under the EPC.
answer_choices.d: The subject matter of the new claims does not diverge considerably from the claims already filed, in particular they should not contain subject matter which has not previously been claimed.

question_text: Which of the following is not a reason for a board to refuse to admit auxiliary requests in appeal proceedings?

answer_choices.a: The requests define subject matter diverging from subject matter of higher ranking requests.
answer_choices.b: The requests were not examined by the first-instance department.
answer_choices.c: The requests were not substantiated.
answer_choices.d: The requests were filed during the oral proceedings.

answer justification: According to the text, the board can refuse to admit auxiliary requests if they define subject matter diverging from subject matter of higher ranking requests, if they were not examined by the first-instance department, or if they are not substantiated. However, the text does not mention that the requests being filed during the oral proceedings is a reason for the board to refuse to admit them.

question_text: Which of the following is a criterion to be taken into account by the boards of appeal when deciding whether a late-filed document is admissible in the appeal proceedings?

answer_choices.a: Whether the document is prima facie highly relevant
answer_choices.b: Whether the document is obviously relevant
answer_choices.c: Whether the document provides a better understanding of the state of the art
answer_choices.d: Whether the document's submission can be seen as reasonable as far as the respondent is concerned

answer justification: According to the text, the boards of appeal consider whether a late-filed document is prima facie highly relevant as a criterion for its admissibility in the appeal proceedings. This means that the document should be highly likely to change the eventual result and is thus highly likely to prejudice the maintenance of the European patent.
source: V.A.5. New submissions on appeal – case law on the RPBA 2007, 1493.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for the boards to refuse to include late-filed evidence of public prior use in the proceedings?

answer_choices.a: The submission is potentially relevant.
answer_choices.b: The submission is filed within the opposition period.
answer_choices.c: The submission is filed after the expiry of the opposition period.
answer_choices.d: The submission is filed with a good reason for the delay.

answer justification: According to the text, the boards have set strict standards for the admissibility of late-filed evidence of public prior use by the opponent. They refuse to include late-filed evidence in the proceedings where it is filed after the expiry of the opposition period. This is the case even if the submission is potentially relevant or filed with a good reason for the delay.
source: Article 114(2) EPC 1973 and case law T 17/91 and T 534/89.

question_text: Which of the following is true about the termination of appeal proceedings in the European Patent Office?

answer_choices.a: The board of appeal can examine the substantive merits of the remaining, limited subject matter if the sole appellant withdraws his appeal.
answer_choices.b: The patent proprietor can force the non-appealing opponent to "live with" a deficiency which he had introduced.
answer_choices.c: The board of appeal can examine the substantive merits of the remaining, limited subject matter if the sole appellant does not withdraw his appeal.
answer_choices.d: The patent had to be granted in its amended form if the sole appellant withdraws his appeal following an allowable limitation of the patent's subject matter under Art. 123 EPC 1973 during appeal proceedings.

answer justification: According to the text, if the sole appellant withdraws his appeal following an allowable limitation of the patent's subject matter under Art. 123 EPC 1973 during appeal proceedings, the patent had to be granted in its amended form.

question_text: What is the primary object of appeal proceedings before the boards of appeal?

answer_choices.b: To review the facts and evidence on which the decision was based

answer_choices.d: To examine the grounds for the contested decision

answer justification: According to the text, the primary object of appeal proceedings is to review the decision under appeal in a judicial manner.

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for remitting a case to the department of first instance according to the text?

question_text: Which of the following is a fundamental procedural deficiency in the first-instance proceedings that amounts to a special reason within the meaning of Art. 11 RPBA 2020 and justifies remittal to the department that issued the contested decision?

answer_choices.a: The department of first instance did not consider all the arguments.
answer_choices.b: The department of first instance did not provide a reasoned decision.
answer_choices.c: The department of first instance violated the right to be heard under Art. 113(1) EPC.
answer_choices.d: The department of first instance did not provide a copy of the decision to the parties.

answer justification: According to the text, a violation of the right to be heard under Art. 113(1) EPC is a fundamental procedural deficiency in the first-instance proceedings that amounts to a special reason within the meaning of Art. 11 RPBA 2020 and justifies remittal to the department that issued the contested decision.
source: Article 11 RPBA 2020 and Case Law of the Bo

question_text: Which of the following is the correct statement about the binding effect of a decision remitting a case to the department of first instance under Article 111(2) EPC?

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for the board to order reimbursement of the appeal fee in the event of a substantial procedural violation?

answer_choices.b: The examining division did not make use of the possibility of granting interlocutory revision after the mistake had been pointed out in the grounds of appeal.
answer_choices.c: The appeal is not allowed and the board finds this equitable by reason of a substantial procedural violation.
answer_choices.d: The grant proceedings had taken longer as a result of a substantial procedural violation.

answer justification: According to the text, a refund of the appeal fee may be ordered under R. 67, second half sentence, EPC 1973, if the appeal is allowed and the board finds this equitable by reason of a substantial procedural violation. Therefore, option A is a reason for the board to order reimbursement of the appeal fee in the event of a substantial procedural violation.

question_text: Which of the following is a procedural violation within the meaning of R. 67 EPC 1973?

answer_choices.a: A failure by the examining division to follow the Guidelines.
answer_choices.b: A failure by the examining division to follow a rule or principle of procedure governed by an Article of the Convention or one of the Implementing Regulations.
answer_choices.c: A failure by the examining division to follow a rule or principle of procedure not governed by an Article of the Convention or one of the Implementing Regulations.
answer_choices.d: A failure by the examining division to follow the Guidelines, but only if it also constitutes a violation of a rule or principle of procedure governed by an Article of the Convention or one of the Implementing Regulations.

answer justification: According to the text, a failure by the examining division to follow a rule or principle of procedure governed by an Article of the Convention or one of the Implementing Regulations is a procedural violation within the meaning of R. 67 EPC 1973. Therefore, option B is the correct answer.

question_text: Which of the following is a procedural violation according to the established jurisprudence of the boards of appeal?

answer_choices.a: A misinterpretation of a document
answer_choices.b: An erroneous assessment of the relevance of a document
answer_choices.c: A wrong assessment of prior art and/or the claimed invention
answer_choices.d: A different opinion on the specialist knowledge to be applied when interpreting the technical content

answer justification: According to the text, a wrong assessment of prior art and/or the claimed invention is considered a substantive error, not a procedural violation.
source: V.A.11. Reimbursement of appeal fees, paragraphs 1543 b and 1544.

question_text: Which of the following is a substantial procedural violation justifying the reimbursement of the appeal fee?

answer_choices.a: A decision taken by a department that is not competent to decide.
answer_choices.b: A decision not approved by all members of the deciding body.
answer_choices.c: A written decision deviating from the oral decision.
answer_choices.d: A decision deviating from a previous communication.

answer_choices.b: Proceedings under Article 112a EPC (petitions for review against decisions of the boards of appeal)

question_text: Which of the following is a valid reason for the Enlarged Board of Appeal to refer a question under Article 112(1)(a) EPC?

answer_choices.d: A lack of uniformity between the boards of appeal and national courts

question_text: Which of the following is a reason for the Enlarged Board of Appeal to refuse a request to suspend appeal proceedings?

answer_choices.c: The appeal proceedings have already been concluded.

question_text: Which of the following is true about petitions for review of interlocutory decisions?

question_text: Which of the following is a necessary condition for a violation of Article 113 EPC to be considered fundamental within the meaning of Article 112a(2)(c) EPC?
